biography: Cédric Oltramare, a name whispered with both promise and frustration in the Ligier JS2 R paddock, hails from the sun-drenched coast of Spain. Born into a family with no racing pedigree, Cédric's passion ignited after a chance encounter with a local karting track at the age of 12. The roar of the engines and the scent of burning rubber became an instant addiction. He quickly rose through the karting ranks, displaying raw speed but also a tendency for costly mistakes. His transition to the Ligier JS2 R series was marked by flashes of brilliance interspersed with baffling inconsistencies. One defining moment was at the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya, where he qualified on pole but spun out on the first lap while battling for the lead. Currently, Cédric is striving to harness his natural talent and transform potential into consistent results. He remains a captivating, if unpredictable, presence on the track, forever chasing that perfect lap.
drivingStyle: Oltramare's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He's known for his aggressive corner entry speeds and late braking maneuvers, often pushing the limits of adhesion. When the car is dialed in, he's capable of breathtaking pace. However, his aggressive style also leads to tire degradation and a higher propensity for errors, especially when under pressure. He struggles to adapt his driving to changing track conditions, preferring to stick to his aggressive baseline setup even when a more conservative approach would yield better results.

careerHighlight: Securing a surprise podium finish at Monza during a rain-soaked race, demonstrating exceptional car control and strategic awareness despite starting from the back of the grid. It was a masterclass in wet weather driving.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead on the final lap of the Valencia race due to excessive oversteer, costing him his first potential victory and earning him criticism for his impetuousness.
